_comment: NEEDS REVIEW: every proverb below is marked "review": "needs review" until a Twi speaker has checked the spelling and translation. When a proverb has been checked, change its review value to "ok". JSON has no comments, so this note and the review field stand in for them.

proverbs.twi: Sɛ wo werɛ fi na wosan kɔfa a, yenkyi.
proverbs.en: It is not wrong to go back for what you forgot.
proverbs.meaning: Learn from the past to build the future (Sankofa).

proverbs.twi: Obi nkyerɛ abofra Nyame.
proverbs.en: No one shows a child the Supreme Being.
proverbs.meaning: God's presence is plain even to a child.

proverbs.twi: Tikoro nkɔ agyina.
proverbs.en: One head does not go into council.
proverbs.meaning: Two heads are better than one; seek advice.

proverbs.twi: Dua koro gye mframa a, ebu.
proverbs.en: A lone tree that faces the wind will break.
proverbs.meaning: There is strength in unity.

proverbs.twi: Nsateaa nyinaa nnyɛ pɛ.
proverbs.en: The fingers are not all equal.
proverbs.meaning: People have different gifts and fortunes.

proverbs.twi: Abaa a wɔde bɔɔ Takyi no, ɛno ara na wɔde bɛbɔ Baah.
proverbs.en: The stick used to beat Takyi is the same one that will beat Baah.
proverbs.meaning: What happens to another can happen to you.

proverbs.twi: Kakra kakra, akokɔ nom nsuo.
proverbs.en: Little by little, the hen drinks water.
proverbs.meaning: Patience and steady effort bring results.

proverbs.twi: Wo foro dua pa a, na yɛpia wo.
proverbs.en: When you climb a good tree, you get a push.
proverbs.meaning: Good causes attract support.

proverbs.twi: Ɔkɔtɔ nwo anomaa.
proverbs.en: A crab does not give birth to a bird.
proverbs.meaning: Children take after their parents.

proverbs.twi: Hu m'ani so ma me nti na atwe mmienu nam.
proverbs.en: Because of 'blow the dust from my eye', two antelopes walk together.
proverbs.meaning: We all need each other.

proverbs.twi: Benkum dware nifa, na nifa nso dware benkum.
proverbs.en: The left hand washes the right, and the right washes the left.
proverbs.meaning: Help one another.

proverbs.twi: Obi nnim obrempɔn ahyɛase.
proverbs.en: No one knows the beginnings of a great person.
proverbs.meaning: Never despise humble beginnings.

proverbs.twi: Ahwenepa nkasa.
proverbs.en: Precious beads do not rattle.
proverbs.meaning: True worth does not need to make noise.

proverbs.twi: Nyansa nni onipa baako ti mu.
proverbs.en: Wisdom is not in one person's head.
proverbs.meaning: No one has all the answers.

proverbs.twi: Ɔba nyansafoɔ, yɛbu no bɛ, yɛnka no asɛm.
proverbs.en: A wise child is spoken to in proverbs, not in plain words.
proverbs.meaning: The wise understand without being told everything.

proverbs.twi: Akokɔ bedeɛ nim adekyeɛ, nanso ɔhwɛ akokɔnini ano.
proverbs.en: The hen knows when dawn comes, but leaves it to the cock to announce.
proverbs.meaning: Respect order and each person's role.

proverbs.twi: Akokɔ nan tia ne ba so a, ɛnkum no.
proverbs.en: When the hen steps on her chick, it does not kill it.
proverbs.meaning: A parent's correction comes from love.

proverbs.twi: Sɛ wo yɔnko abɔdwesɛ rehye a, sa nsuo bɔ wo deɛ ho.
proverbs.en: When your friend's beard is on fire, keep water by your own.
proverbs.meaning: Learn from the troubles of others.

proverbs.twi: Ɔbaa na ɔwoo ɔbarima.
proverbs.en: It is a woman who gave birth to a man.
proverbs.meaning: Honour women.

proverbs.twi: Nnipa nyinaa yɛ Nyame mma; obi nnyɛ asaase ba.
proverbs.en: All people are children of God; no one is a child of the earth.
proverbs.meaning: Every person has equal dignity.

proverbs.twi: Abofra bɔ nwa, na ɔmmɔ akyekyedeɛ.
proverbs.en: A child may crack a snail's shell, but not a tortoise's.
proverbs.meaning: Know your limits.

proverbs.twi: Obi mfa ne benkum nkyerɛ n'agya kurom.
proverbs.en: No one points to their father's village with the left hand.
proverbs.meaning: Respect your roots.

proverbs.twi: Aboa a onni dua, Nyame na ɔpra ne ho.
proverbs.en: For the animal without a tail, God brushes off the flies.
proverbs.meaning: God cares for the vulnerable.

proverbs.twi: Ahoɔfɛ ntua ka.
proverbs.en: Beauty does not pay debts.
proverbs.meaning: Character and hard work matter more than looks.

proverbs.twi: Woamma wo yɔnko antwa nkron a, wo nso worentwa du.
proverbs.en: If you don't let your neighbour reach nine, you will never reach ten.
proverbs.meaning: Help others rise, and you rise too.

proverbs.twi: Ɔwɔ aka me nti, mehunu sonsono a, misuro.
proverbs.en: Because a snake bit me, I fear even an earthworm.
proverbs.meaning: Once bitten, twice shy.

proverbs.twi: Anomaa antu a, ɔbua da.
proverbs.en: The bird that does not fly goes to bed hungry.
proverbs.meaning: No effort, no reward.

proverbs.twi: Tete wɔ bi ka, tete wɔ bi kyerɛ.
proverbs.en: The ancients have something to say and something to teach.
proverbs.meaning: Value the wisdom of tradition.

proverbs.twi: Abofra hunu ne nsa hohoro a, ɔne mpanimfoɔ didi.
proverbs.en: When a child learns to wash their hands, they eat with the elders.
proverbs.meaning: Good conduct earns respect.

proverbs.twi: Kwaterekwa se ɔbɛma wo ntoma a, tie ne din.
proverbs.en: When a naked man offers you cloth, listen to his name.
proverbs.meaning: Judge a promise by the one who makes it.
